subject: Post-demo: SDK onboarding + reranker / request-response contract questions
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Torres <eve@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SDK onboarding + reranker / request-response contract questions

Hi Eve — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from our side:
- You want a light integration path via our SDK for inference requests, with the option to call our reranker endpoint for n-best reordering.
- Primary constraints: client-side token accounting (Helix enforces a 1M token/month cap for their pilot) and server-side stop/streaming semantics for real-time chat UI.

Open technical questions we promised to follow up on (high priority):
1) SDK auth model: do you want OAuth2 service accounts (recommended for server-side) or API key per environment? We can support both but need to align for token rotation and secrets management.
2) Reranker contract: what format do you expect for candidates? We propose a JSON list of {id, score, raw_text, embedding_vector?} — want to confirm whether you need vectors sent or just ids + text.
3) Chat vs completions: do your clients need streaming token-by-token updates, or are you fine waiting for a finished completion? Streaming implies websocket/HTTP2 and different client UX.
4) Stop sequences / max_tokens: are you enforcing a strict token ceiling per user request? If so, we will implement server-side guard rails and report back on truncation behavior.

Next steps:
- If you can, reply with preferred auth model and whether Helix will accept server-managed keys.
- Marissa from our integration team will share a short spec and sample payloads by EOD Monday.
- We’ll attach a first-draft integration spec (see attachment) with concrete request/response examples.

Attachments: helix_integration_spec_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

— Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK onboarding + reranker / request-response contract questions

Hi Eve — following up with the brief spec I promised. I pasted two representative examples below (chat + rerank). The attached PDF has the complete set. Please confirm which variant you prefer and any fields you absolutely need preserved.

Example A — chat (streaming off):
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>
Body JSON:
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-4x",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the transcript."}],
  "max_tokens": 1200,
  "stop": ["

User:"],
  "stream": false
}

Server response (single JSON):
{
  "id": "cmpl-...",
  "choices": [{"message": {"role":"assistant","content":"Short summary..."}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 120, "completion_tokens": 85, "total_tokens": 205}

Notes: If you need deterministic truncation behavior, set max_tokens on the client and we will return total_tokens and a clear finish_reason ("length") when truncated.

Example B — reranker call (batch re-ranking of 10 candidates):
POST /v1/rerank
Body JSON:
{
  "query": "What is the best way to connect Redwood?",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"Use SDK A..."},
    {"id":"c2","text":"Embed + index..."}
  ],
  "return_vectors": false 
}

Response:
{
  "ranks": [{"id":"c2","score":0.93},{"id":"c1","score":0.42}],
  "timing_ms": 48
}

Key questions for Helix:
- For rerank candidates, do you prefer we accept precomputed vectors (embedding arrays) or raw text only? Accepting vectors offloads compute from us but requires Helix to manage vector serialization and precision (float32 vs float16).
- Do you want our SDK to expose a single unified call that performs generate->embed->rerank under the hood? That simplifies client code but is heavier in latency.

Operational notes:
- Auth: service-account tokens (JWTs) enable short-lived creds and rotate automatically with KMS/HSM integration. If you require per-developer API keys for audit trail, we can enable both with different scopes.
- Streaming: our SDK has a streaming client that opens a single HTTP/2 stream and yields token deltas. Fallback to polling is available but increases latency.

Please reply with which of the above you want us to prototype first (auth + rerank candidate format vs streaming chat UX).

— Marissa Cole
Integration Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Eve Torres <eve@helixlabs.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helix Labs Integrations <integration@helixlabs.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK onboarding + reranker / request-response contract questions

Hi Monica and Marissa — thanks for the quick follow. A few clarifications from Helix: 

1) Auth: for the pilot we prefer a service account model (server-to-server). We will need per-environment scopes (dev/stage/prod) and the ability to rotate without downtime.

2) Reranker candidates: we prefer to send raw text + candidate id only. Helix will host an embeddings pipeline later, but for now we want Redwood to take the text and return scores. Send us the JSON example you used above as the canonical shape.

3) Streaming: our chat UI team wants streaming token deltas. Can you confirm expected client-side reconnection semantics if a stream drops? Also: does your SDK provide partial choice IDs while streaming (so we can start rendering candidate highlights)?

4) Tokens: Helix enforces per-user soft caps in the client. We need Redwood to return clear usage fields in every response (prompt/completion/total) and an explicit finish_reason when truncated. If you have a webhooks endpoint for usage alerts, that would be helpful.

Last note: can you include a minimal example of a websocket handshake for streaming in the spec? Marissa — if you can add that and indicate retry semantics, we can approve the pilot scope this week.

Thanks,

Eve Torres
Head of Integrations, Helix Labs

Hi team — quick operational plan based on Helix answers: 

- Marissa: I’ll ask you to attach a one-page websocket handshake + reconnection table to the spec (retry backoff, idempotency token semantics). Also indicate whether partial-choice IDs are emitted during streaming and what the schema looks like (we can emit incremental choice objects).
- Monica: I’ll prepare a short SOW addendum covering service-account provisioning and key rotation timelines so Helix can share with their security team.
- Action items for Helix: confirm the webhook URL for usage alerts (Eve, please share) and confirm dev/stage/prod environment names so we can create scoped tokens.

I’ve attached a compact post-demo doc with the decisions we made and the immediate next steps for legal and onboarding.
